extra_misconceptions.fact: Plaster cures underwater through a chemical reaction and will solidify inside the drain trap, permanently blocking the plumbing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring leftover liquid plaster down a studio sink drain with plenty of cold water flushes the pipes cleanly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dull blades require excessive force and slip unpredictably off the wood grain, whereas sharp tools cut cleanly with controlled pressure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dull woodcarving gouge is safer for beginners to use than a razor-sharp blade because it cuts skin less easily.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fine silica dust penetrates woven cloth masks easily, so sculptors must wear a NIOSH-approved N95 or P100 particulate respirator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard cloth face coverings block airborne crystalline silica particles produced when rasping dry clay or alabaster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Curing plaster releases intense exothermic heat above 140 degrees Fahrenheit that can cause severe thermal burns and trap the hand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soaking a hand coated in wet plaster of Paris lets you create a direct life-cast mold without any thermal hazard.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Adult human eyes sit halfway between the crown of the head and the bottom of the chin; the forehead and hair occupy the upper half.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Human eyes sit roughly one-third of the way down from the top of the skull on a life-size portrait sculpture.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Oil-based clay contains waxes and oils that melt and burn when heated; only water-based ceramic clay can be fired in a kiln.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Oil-based plastilina modeling clay hardens permanently when baked inside a ceramic kiln just like stoneware clay.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sifting dry plaster powder into measured water lets each particle soak evenly and prevents dry lumps and trapped air bubbles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring water directly into a bucket of dry plaster powder mixes a smooth, bubble-free batch of casting plaster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trapped moisture inside thick solid clay turns to steam during firing and causes the sculpture to explode unless hollowed out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A solid six-inch sphere of water-based ceramic clay can go straight into a kiln once the outer surface feels dry.

extra_socratic_questions: What physical indicator on the water surface shows you have sifted enough dry plaster powder before mixing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many sculptors work in industrial design, medical prosthetics, toy prototyping, film effects, and 3D video game character modeling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional sculptors work only in fine-art galleries creating standalone stone or bronze statues for collectors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Studios and clients evaluate a sculptor primarily through a curated portfolio demonstrating anatomy, form, and technical execution.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Bachelor of Fine Arts degree is the only credential that matters when applying for studio or digital sculpting jobs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Digital sculpting software replicates physical clay tools, so convincing 3D forms still depend on anatomy, proportion, and gesture.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital sculptors using 3D software no longer need to study traditional human anatomy or physical weight balance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skin oils, sweat, and salts chemically corrode bronze patinas over time, leaving permanent etched fingerprints and discolored spots.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Touching a bronze sculpture in a museum gallery is harmless because solid metal cannot be damaged by human fingers.
